newsitem.title: UK: IBCA rates Council of Europe Social Fund.
newsitem.headline: IBCA rates Council of Europe Social Fund.

text.p: IBCA, the European rating agency, said on Wednesday it had assigned a long-term rating of AAA to the 3.0 billion Ecu programme for the issuance of debt instruments of the Council of Europe Social Development Fund (CEF).
"The Fund, an international development bank that grants loans to its members, is the financial tool of the Council of Europe's social policy," IBCA said in a statement.
IBCA said 25 European countries are members of the Fund, and France, Germany and Italy are the main shareholders with 18.3 percent each.

"It is a separate legal entity from the Council of Europe, with its own financial resources, i.e. the capital subscribed by members, equity reserves and borrowings on the capital markets," the agency said.
It said AAA rated countries hold almost 44 percent of CEF's subscribed capital and investment grade shareholders (BBB- rating or above) 90 percent.

"The consensus between the Fund's members and its political independence vis-a-vis its larger shareholders are among its strengths. Over time its members have shown their commitment to the Fund, both by agreeing to raise new capital and by their consistent support of its Governing Board," IBCA said.

"CEF's currently pursues its purpose to help in solving the social problems with which European countries are faced by providing loans for social housing, small-and medium-sized corporates, schools and hospitals," it said. "Its loan portfolio is overwhelmingly sovereign risk."
IBCA said the Governor and most of the senior management of CEF has changed since December 1993.
"Profit maximisation is not one of the Fund's goals, yet operating results have been satisfactory."

"The rating takes into account CEF's generally sound financial results and structure, the loan diversification management is currently pursuing and the credit standing of its shareholders," IBCA said.
